Mean validation-selected C-indices for TopoHyperClinicalGraph versus pathology-only spatial PatchGCN were 0.7563 versus 0.7386 in COADREAD, 0.6220 versus 0.5998 in HNSC, 0.6755 versus 0.6535 in BRCA and 0.6409 versus 0.6176 in STAD. CPTAC scores were 0.5984 in HNSC, 0.6060 in PDA, 0.8055 in CCRCC and 0.7192 in LUAD. CPTAC-HNSC used TCGA-initialized adaptation; other CPTAC backbones were trained within their cohorts. Geometry accounted for most pathology-only gains, with smaller persistence effects. Clinical graph fusion exceeded its matched node-wise control in five cohorts, tied in one and scored lower in two; clinical-only prediction exceeded fusion in three CPTAC cohorts. The framework supports separate evaluation of geometric, topological and clinical contributions. All scores were validation-selected; independent testing is needed to establish generalizability.
item.dc:creator: Noaman Khan, Zubair Shah

item.title: Enhancing Medical Lesion Segmentation via Several Simple Modules
item.description: arXiv:2610.41652v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This work introduces three lightweight enhancement modules for medical lesion segmentation to improve clinical applicability, particularly under data-scarce and computationally constrained environments. Current mainstream methods struggle with the lack of high-quality annotations for rare pathologies, which often leads to severe morphological distortions during inference, despite achieving seemingly ideal DSC scores. Furthermore, the isolated development of individual segmentation tasks restricts cross-domain methodological innovation, underscoring the need for leveraging shared knowledge across different lesions within the same anatomical region. However, constrained access to historical data and annotations hinders efficient knowledge extraction and triggers catastrophic forgetting when adapting to new classes. To address these challenges, we first propose DT-Morph Combined Loss with continuous spatial pooling to optimize differentiable topological structures and boundary continuity. Second, we introduce 3D Group Prompt, which extracts domain-universal knowledge via curated volumetric image-mask alignment prompts together with text prompts built on SAT baseline. Finally, we replace conventional output layers with Many-to-One Conditional Segmentation Head equipped with synonym-resolved routing, which brings negligible computational cost and enables fast incremental learning for new categories without sacrificing performance on old tasks. Ablation studies on abdominal and extra-abdominal datasets covering both organ and lesion segmentation verify the efficacy of our modules.
item.dc:creator: Ruichen Li, Zhao Yao

item.title: OpenVIO: A Versatile Open-Source Visual-Inertial Odometry System
item.description: arXiv:2610.41671v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Visual-inertial odometry (VIO) is a fundamental topic in robotics research. Beyond research, VIO has been adopted in a wide range of products. In this manuscript, we present OpenVIO, an open-source VIO system for research and practical applications. It is released under the MIT license. OpenVIO supports pinhole and fisheye cameras and extends this support to stitched 360{\deg} images. We describe each part of the system together with its design considerations. We also report benchmark results with other open-source VIO systems on public datasets. OpenVIO is available as open source at https://github.com/93won/openvio.
item.dc:creator: Seungwon Choi

item.title: ReuScope: Auditing Data Reuse and Evaluation Sensitivity in Capsule Vision 2024
item.description: arXiv:2610.41835v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop ReuScope, a protocol for auditing data reuse and evaluation sensitivity, using Capsule Vision 2024 as a case study. It combines measurements of data relationships with two comparisons: changing the evaluation population while holding predictions fixed, and changing training data while holding evaluation fixed. Byte-identical files cross the public training-validation boundary, and all 41 Kvasir-Capsule recordings that contribute frames occur in both partitions. Shared source recordings establish cross-split overlap; missing cross-recording patient identifiers prevent counting unique shared patients. Across ten paired seeds, removing all training rows attributed to Kvasir-Capsule, plus five rows from other sources flagged as near-matches to it, lowers public-validation balanced accuracy from 82.5% to 61.2%. Evaluating the same fitted models on the validation rows of the other sources reverses the comparison: removal improves balanced accuracy by 1.38 percentage points. The public-validation drop measures sensitivity to source removal, not an amount of leakage-induced inflation. Matched controls show that sample size and class counts alone do not explain the observed score differences. An exploratory experiment removes the training neighbors of validation frames that have close training matches, or equally many distant training rows, and yields a difference-in-differences estimate, relative to matched unflagged frames, of -0.355 percentage points in true-class probability; the paired-t interval for accuracy spans zero. The resulting procedure distinguishes observed reuse from conditional performance sensitivity and specifies the population, class support and uncertainty unit for each conclusion.
item.dc:creator: Eunseob Choi, Kyeonghun Kim, Hyuk-Jae Lee, Nam-Joon Kim

item.title: Movens-Zero: Scaling Humanoid Motion Foundation Models with Large-Scale Human Videos
item.description: arXiv:2610.41877v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scaling humanoid motion foundation models is constrained by the scarcity of diverse, robot-executable data and by the difficulty of jointly learning from heterogeneous multimodal inputs while supporting real-time closed-loop control. We present Movens-5M, constructed from raw Internet videos through clip generation, quality filtering, semantic annotation, motion recovery, and physical refinement with humanoid retargeting and execution verification. It contains 15 million human-motion sequences and 5 million physically executable humanoid-motion sequences spanning over 10,000 hours, aligned with text, RGB video, speech, and music. Building on this data, we introduce Movens-Zero, a scalable understanding-generation-execution architecture that supports joint learning across modalities and real-time closed-loop execution. Task-mixed flow-matching training jointly optimizes a single action expert across seven generation tasks, enabling direct motion generation from text, speech, music, and video. Multimodal Real-Time Chunking connects overlapping chunks under continuously updated instructions and robot states for continuous closed-loop execution. We further introduce Movens-Intent, a four-track benchmark with 8,192 expert-verified condition-motion pairs across text, speech, music, and video. Experiments show consistent gains across all four modalities when scaling execution-verified data from 1% to 100% and action-expert capacity from 64M to 911M parameters, while demonstrating that data quality and cross-modal supervision improve generation and execution.
item.dc:creator: Wendong Bu, Tinghong Ye, Qizhou Wang, Jiacheng Li, Zhiqi Ge, Yuze Lin, Zhongqi Yue, Yi Su, Jingyu Wang, Kai Shen, Jingdong Liu, Chengyuan Deng, Xiaoxuan Chen, Xin Tan, Jiaming Ji, Wenqiao Zhang, Chenghong Jiang, Tuoyu Li, Siliang Tang, Jun Xiao, Tat-Seng Chua, Yueting Zhuang, Xingxing Wang, Juncheng Li

item.title: IGDA-ICMH: an Importance Guided Feature and Network Dual Adaptation Framework towards Image Compression for Machine and Human Vision
item.description: arXiv:2610.41924v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: With the surge of machine vision applications, image compression for both machine and human vision (ICMH) has become an important research area. Existing studies mainly focus on task-specific adaptation or multi-task joint optimization, yet they often overlook the unequal contributions of different features and network layers to downstream machine vision tasks. To address this issue, we first quantitatively investigate the impact of different feature and network layers on machine vision performance, providing a principled understanding of their importance. Based on this analysis, an Importance Guided feature and network Dual Adaptation (IGDA) framework is developed for ICMH. It adopts implicit neural representation as the basic architecture and designs an efficient adaptation structure with both feature and network weight adaptation. An Importance-Guided Network Adaptation (IGNA) module is developed with a low-rank adaptation strategy to selectively adjust key network layers according to their importance in different tasks. An Importance-Guided Feature Adaptation (IGFA) module is developed with a low-rank and Kronecker product-based transform to explore the non-local property of the features in order to reduce the number of adaptation parameters. Extensive experiments on representative machine vision tasks, including image classification and object detection, demonstrate that our IGDA-ICMH framework achieves significantly better performance than the existing implicit neural representation-based methods for ICMH.
item.dc:creator: Yanbo Gao, Xinyu Zhao, Shuai Li, Xun Cai, Mao Ye, Li Li

item.title: REA: A Routed Embodied Agent Runtime for Asynchronous Brain-Cerebellum Control
item.description: arXiv:2610.42053v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Foundation models are becoming remarkably reliable at high-level reasoning, yet they remain too slow and costly to serve as fine-grained controllers. Conversely, fast policies like VLAs and whole-body controllers offer more efficient reflexes, but struggle to generalize. While pairing a deliberative brain (foundation models) with a reactive cerebellum (fast policies) seems natural for embodied systems, two obstacles remain: methods are built and scored on incompatible stacks, and their asynchronous coordination is difficult. For example, an agent that calls the VLA in the agentic loop can stall the fast execution, while a VLA that calls the agent on errors tends to re-trigger fallbacks repeatedly or completely miss silent failures. To address this, we propose REA (Routed Embodied Agent), a unified runtime where a deliberative System 2, an embodied router System 1 and reactive System 0 policies cooperate under a single golden rule - no running policy waits on the brain. Instead of querying the brain at each failure, REA employs a route memory that stores each policy's measured success ahead of time, a boundary-triggered judge gate that consults the brain on policy execution, and a shared-budget escalation ladder for bounded recovery. Evaluated on 3,000 test episodes across 60 LIBERO-Pro tasks, REA reaches 95.9% success and beats the best single-agent baseline in its own policy pool (94.7%) while reducing control steps by 25% and control time by 17%. In a separate 100-episode RoboTwin 2.0 study, REA achieves 84% success with VLA policies and 86% with VLA+code, compared with 80% for the strongest single VLA baseline MEDex. These results demonstrate learned and programmatic policies operating within the same runtime. REA also transfers to BEHAVIOR-1K and a real Unitree G1 humanoid, achieving the highest observed success among the compared methods.
item.dc:creator: Pengfei Zhou, Yixing Ma, Zhengfeiyang Zhang, Haoyuan Chen, Zhenglin Wan, Hexin Wang, Wangbo Zhao, Yang You

item.title: RoboArchitect: Automating the Design of Robotic Agents with Persistent Memory
item.description: arXiv:2610.42141v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent work shows that a frozen robot policy performs far better inside an agent harness, where control code decides when to query the policy, consult vision tools, or command the arm directly. Yet today these harnesses are built by hand and redesigned for each new robot or benchmark. We show that harness design can be automated, offering a strong alternative to finetuning on a novel setup. In RoboArchitect, a coding model observes a robot's rollouts, diagnoses failures, and iteratively revises the harness around the frozen policy. The harness evolves on a set of episodes for its optimization and is evaluated on held-out scenes and tasks. Without updating any model weights, RoboArchitect raises average success from 9.7% to 43.3% on unseen scenes (4.5x) and from 12.7% to 40.2% on unseen tasks (3.2x), across multiple benchmarks and policies. The gains are largest where the benchmark is far from the policy's training data: wrapping a general-purpose policy, the evolved harness yields a specialist that often outperforms even the finetuned version. Intuitive control strategies are automatically designed, such as lifting a jammed arm clear or reaching in horizontally when an obstacle blocks the way from above. The harness also evolves its own persistent memory, carrying learned experience, such as effective grasp depths, into later decisions. These results suggest that substantial headroom in robotic manipulation lies in the agent harness, and its design can be effectively automated and optimized without weight updates.
item.dc:creator: Shengguang Wu, Suning Huang, Cherie Ho, Ria Doshi, Hao Zhu, Serena Yeung-Levy

item.title: SemEllipsoid: Semantic-aware Shape Abstraction with Ellipsoid
item.description: arXiv:2610.42145v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Representing 3D shapes using a set of primitives - known as shape abstraction - is an actively studied problem in computer graphics with wide applications in shape understanding, analysis, and simulation due to the compactness and computational efficiency of the primitive-based representation. Prior work has primarily focused on geometry-aware shape abstraction, where the objective is to approximate the input shape with a minimal set of primitives while preserving geometric fidelity. However, these methods often overlook semantic consistency, inevitably leading to primitives that span across multiple semantic parts. Such inconsistency can cause undesirable artifacts in downstream tasks such as part-level shape editing or manipulation. In this paper, we introduce a new task - semantic-aware shape abstraction, where the goal is to produce abstractions that are both geometrically faithful and semantically consistent, ensuring that each primitive adheres strictly to a single semantic part without crossing semantic boundaries. We propose SemEllipsoid, a novel method to address this problem using ellipsoidal primitives. The core idea is to inject semantic constraints into the primitive optimization process leveraging the availability of semantic cues from large-scale foundation models. We design a fully differentiable projection-blending-evaluation scheme to measure semantic divergence against input semantic masks, and formulate an alternating optimization strategy to iteratively solve for optimal semantic assignment and primitive configurations. Our method is non-learning-based, requiring no data collection or network training, and generalizes well to shapes from arbitrary categories. It also supports different levels of abstraction according to user demand. Extensive experiments and evaluations validate the effectiveness of our approach across several 3D shape collections.
item.dc:creator: Kuankuan Cheng, Haocheng Yuan, Changjian Li

item.title: point2vec for Self-Supervised Representation Learning on Point Clouds
item.description: arXiv:2303.16570v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present point2vec, a self-supervised method for learning point cloud representations through masked prediction of a teacher network's latent features. Building on data2vec, we investigate a limitation of applying this approach to point clouds: positional information associated with masked patches reveals the overall object shape to the student, weakening the learning task even under heavy masking. point2vec addresses this issue by passing only visible patches to the student encoder and introducing a shallow decoder to predict representations for masked patches. The teacher processes the complete point cloud to provide contextualized training targets. These targets capture global context through the teacher's self-attention, providing supervision beyond the local geometry of individual patches. This design conceals masked-patch positions from the student and reduces its computational cost during pre-training. Our ablations show that the decoder alone provides only part of the improvement; concealing positional information is key. After pre-training on ShapeNet, point2vec outperforms the evaluated self-supervised baselines on shape classification on ModelNet40 and ScanObjectNN and few-shot classification on ModelNet40, while achieving competitive part segmentation results on ShapeNetPart.
item.dc:creator: Karim Knaebel, Jonas Schult, Alexander Hermans, Bastian Leibe

item.title: Position: Next-Generation Game Engines Should Be Built on Interactive Generative Video
item.description: arXiv:2503.17359v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Modern game development faces significant challenges in creativity and cost due to predetermined content in traditional game engines. Recent breakthroughs in video generation models, capable of synthesizing realistic and interactive virtual environments, present an opportunity to revolutionize game creation. This position paper argues that next-generation game engines should be built on Interactive Generative Video (IGV). We term such engines Generative Game Engines (GGE), with IGV as the perceptual and world-generation core under designer control. We argue why IGV is uniquely suited for this role, identify what is missing, and examine progress across six functional modules to show how each supports our position, culminating in a five-level maturity roadmap (L0-L4). Drawing on discussions with researchers, game developers, and community participants, we present nine alternative views and ethical considerations to stimulate debate.
item.dc:creator: Jiwen Yu, Yiran Qin, Haoxuan Che, Quande Liu, Xintao Wang, Pengfei Wan, Di Zhang, Xihui Liu

item.title: Denoising Mutual Knowledge Distillation in Bi-Directional Multiple Instance Learning
item.description: arXiv:2505.12074v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multiple Instance Learning is the predominant method for Whole Slide Image classification in digital pathology, enabling the use of slide-level labels to supervise model training. Although MIL eliminates the tedious fine-grained annotation process for supervised learning, whether it can learn accurate bag- and instance-level classifiers remains a question. To address the issue, instance-level classifiers and instance masks were incorporated to ground the prediction on supporting patches. These methods, while practically improving the performance of MIL methods, may potentially introduce noisy labels. We propose to bridge the gap between commonly used MIL and fully supervised learning by augmenting both the bag- and instance-level learning processes with pseudo-label correction capabilities elicited from weak to strong generalization techniques. The proposed algorithm improves the performance of dual-level MIL algorithms on both bag- and instance-level predictions. Experiments on public pathology datasets showcase the advantage of the proposed methods.
item.dc:creator: Chen Shu, Boyu Fu, Yiman Li, Ting Yin, Wenchuan Zhang, Jie Chen, Yuhao Yi, Hong Bu

item.title: VisualSphinx: Large-Scale Synthetic Vision Logic Puzzles for RL
item.description: arXiv:2505.23977v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Vision language models (VLMs) are expected to perform effective multimodal reasoning and make logically coherent decisions, which is critical to tasks such as diagram understanding and spatial problem solving. However, current VLM reasoning lacks large-scale and well-structured training datasets. To bridge this gap, we propose VisualSphinx, a first-of-its-kind large-scale synthetic visual logical reasoning training dataset. To tackle the challenge of image synthesis with grounded answers, we propose a rule-to-image synthesis pipeline that extracts and expands puzzle rules from seed questions and generates executable rendering programs for puzzle assembly. Using standard GRPO with binary correctness rewards as a validation recipe, experiments show that VLMs trained on VisualSphinx benefit from the logical coherence and readability of our dataset and exhibit improved performance on logical reasoning tasks. The enhanced reasoning capabilities developed from VisualSphinx also benefit other reasoning tasks such as algebraic reasoning, arithmetic reasoning and geometry reasoning.
item.dc:creator: Yichen Feng, Zhangchen Xu, Fengqing Jiang, Yuetai Li, Bhaskar Ramasubramanian, Luyao Niu, Bill Yuchen Lin, Radha Poovendran

item.title: PPS: Plug-and-Play Saccadic Vision for Fine-Grained Classification
item.description: arXiv:2509.15688v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fine-grained visual classification benefits from high-resolution inputs to resolve subtle, localized cues, but at the cost of large compute and memory budgets. Inspired by human saccadic vision, we propose a lightweight extension that turns any pretrained backbone with spatial feature maps into a saccadic classifier through glimpse-induced inference. The only architectural additions are a small priority head and a single cross-attention fusion block. The same weight-tied encoder encodes a downsampled peripheral glance, exposes the spatial feature map from which the priority head predicts a glimpse-priority distribution and re-encodes high-resolution glimpse crops sampled from that distribution in parallel. A sequential sampler with non-maximum suppression draws a runtime-configurable number of glimpses. A residual multi-head cross-attention block then fuses the glance against the glimpses. To improve the quality of the priority maps, we train the priority head by a per-glimpse information-gain target from a lightweight per-image memory bank. This requires no reinforcement learning. Complexity is linear in the number of glimpses and peak memory is decoupled from input resolution. Across nine benchmarks our framework improves consistently over its backbones.
item.dc:creator: Johann Schmidt, Sebastian Stober, Joachim Denzler, Paul Bodesheim

item.title: On the Faithfulness of Visual Thinking: Measurement and Enhancement
item.description: arXiv:2510.23482v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent large vision-language models (LVLMs) can generate vision-text multimodal chain-of-thought (MCoT) traces after reinforcement fine-tuning (RFT). However, we observe that the visual information in MCoT is often inaccurate even when answers are correct, and task accuracy remains nearly unchanged despite the visual information being corrupted. This indicates a lack of faithfulness in the vision part of MCoT reasoning. We attribute this to the RL reward design in RFT, which solely incentivizes the format of interleaved vision-text cues, encouraging the model to incorporate visual information into its text reasoning steps without considering its correctness. In this paper, we first probe MCoT faithfulness by measuring how much the prediction changes when its visual and textual thoughts are intervened. Surprisingly, the model's predictions remain nearly unchanged under visual intervention but change significantly under textual intervention, indicating that the visual evidence is largely ignored. To further analyze the visual information, we introduce an automated LVLM-based evaluation metric that quantifies the faithfulness of visual cues from two perspectives: relevance and sufficiency. Our evaluation reveals that the visual information in current MCoT traces is simultaneously irrelevant and insufficient. To address this issue, we propose Sufficient-Component Cause Model (SCCM) learning. This approach encourages the MCoT to generate sufficient yet minimal visual components that are independently capable of leading to the correct answer. The proposed SCCM is annotation-free and plug-and-play, compatible with various RFT for MCoT. Empirical results demonstrate that SCCM substantially improves the visual faithfulness across a suite of fine-grained perception and reasoning benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/EugeneLiu01/Faithful_Thinking_with_Image.
item.dc:creator: Zujing Liu, Junwen Pan, Qi She, Yuan Gao, Guisong Xia

item.title: MIC-BEV: Multi-Infrastructure Camera Bird's-Eye-View Transformer with Relation-Aware Fusion for 3D Object Detection
item.description: arXiv:2510.24688v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Infrastructure-based perception plays a crucial role in intelligent transportation systems by providing global situational awareness and enabling cooperative autonomy. However, camera-based 3D object detection remains challenging under multi-view infrastructure setups, heterogeneous camera configurations, degraded sensing conditions, diverse road layouts, and adverse environmental conditions. We introduce MIC-BEV, a Transformer-based bird's-eye-view (BEV) perception framework for infrastructure-based multi-camera 3D object detection. MIC-BEV supports a variable number of cameras with heterogeneous intrinsic and extrinsic parameters and uses a graph-enhanced fusion module to adaptively integrate multi-view image features by modeling geometric relationships between cameras and the BEV grid. To support training and evaluation, we introduce M2I, a synthetic dataset featuring diverse camera layouts, road geometries, environmental conditions, and sensor-degradation cases. Experiments on the simulated M2I dataset and the real-world RoScenes dataset show that MIC-BEV achieves strong 3D detection performance and improved robustness under challenging conditions. Ablation studies validate the effectiveness of its key design choices, while weight analyses show that the learned fusion weights are associated with view-reliability factors and adapt to degraded camera inputs. We further report computational cost and deployment-related factors, providing additional evidence of practical feasibility and real-world deployment potential. These results indicate that MIC-BEV is a promising framework for infrastructure-based perception. The dataset and source code are available at: https://github.com/HandsomeYun/MIC-BEV.
item.dc:creator: Yun Zhang, Zhaoliang Zheng, Johnson Liu, Zhiyu Huang, Zewei Zhou, Zonglin Meng, Tianhui Cai, Jiaqi Ma

item.title: NP-LoRA: Null Space Projection for Subject-Style LoRA Fusion
item.description: arXiv:2511.11051v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fusion enables the composition of subject and style representations for controllable generation without retraining. However, existing approaches primarily operate through weight-level merging, without explicitly modeling how independently trained LoRAs interact in the shared parameter space. We adopt a geometric perspective on LoRA fusion, interpreting content and style LoRAs as occupying overlapping, non-orthogonal low-rank subspaces, where such overlap can lead to conflicting parameter updates that affect generation quality. This observation motivates us to reformulate LoRA fusion not merely as parameter combination, but as a problem of controlling how updates from overlapping subspaces are combined. Based on this insight, we propose Null Space Projection LoRA (NP-LoRA), a training-free framework that employs projection as a fusion operator to explicitly modulate cross-LoRA interactions. Specifically, NP-LoRA uses principal directions of the style LoRA to define a projection subspace and projects the content LoRA onto the complementary subspace (i.e., the null space of the style LoRA), suppressing interference along dominant style directions while preserving complementary information. To avoid the overly aggressive suppression of hard projection, we further formulate soft projection as a regularized optimization problem that balances content preservation against style-subspace suppression. This objective admits a closed-form solution, yielding a projection operator controlled by a single parameter that continuously interpolates between linear merging and hard projection. Extensive experiments across multiple pretrained LoRA pairs show that NP-LoRA achieves more balanced content-style composition compared to strong baselines, without requiring retraining. Code is available at https://github.com/blackzebra7/NP-LoRA.
item.dc:creator: Chuheng Chen, Xiaofei Zhou, Geyuan Zhang, Yong Huang, Gang Xiong

item.title: DiTGaze: Geometry-Conditioned Diffusion Augmentation for Few-Shot Gaze Estimation
item.description: arXiv:2511.11231v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Accurate person-specific gaze estimation benefits from labeled user data, but collecting images that densely cover gaze directions is burdensome. We present DiTGaze, a calibration-efficient augmentation system that follows a two-stream 3D Gaussian Splatting backbone and reformulates its convolutional rendering stage as a geometry-conditioned latent Diffusion Transformer (DiT). A learnable projection and frozen VAE bridge rasterized Gaussian features to latent tokens, while timestep and identity/expression conditioning are integrated through Adaptive Layer Normalization. Intermediate yaw-pitch sampling densifies gaze supervision, and an orthogonality constraint reduces interference between gaze, pose, and expression. On ETH-XGaze, DiTGaze reduces generator-level gaze error by 4.1 percent relative to GazeGaussian. In our runs of the expanded downstream protocol, it ranks first at every calibration budget from one to nine real images; the repeated primary comparison at N = 9 reduces subject-level estimator error by 0.73 degrees and improves 14 of 15 identities (p < 0.001). These results connect the proposed generator changes to statistically supported few-shot personalization gains.
item.dc:creator: Abiram Panchalingam, Indu P. Bodala, Stuart E. Middleton

item.title: Differential Vector Erasure: Unified Training-Free Concept Erasure for Flow Matching Models
item.description: arXiv:2602.01089v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Text-to-image diffusion models have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in generating high-quality images, yet their tendency to reproduce undesirable concepts, such as NSFW content, copyrighted styles, or specific objects, poses growing concerns for safe and controllable deployment. While existing concept erasure approaches primarily focus on DDPM-based diffusion models and rely on costly fine-tuning, the recent emergence of flow matching models introduces a fundamentally different generative paradigm for which prior methods are not directly applicable. In this paper, we propose Differential Vector Erasure (DVE), a training-free concept erasure method specifically designed for flow matching models. Our key insight is that semantic concepts are implicitly encoded in the directional structure of the velocity field governing the generative flow. Leveraging this observation, we construct a differential vector field that characterizes the directional discrepancy between a target concept and a carefully chosen anchor concept. During inference, DVE selectively removes concept-specific components by projecting the velocity field onto the differential direction, enabling precise concept suppression without affecting irrelevant semantics. Extensive experiments on FLUX demonstrate that DVE consistently outperforms existing baselines on a wide range of concept erasure tasks, including NSFW suppression, artistic style removal, and object erasure, while preserving image quality and diversity. Code is available at https://github.com/zhiqizhang23/DVE.
item.dc:creator: Zhiqi Zhang, Xinhao Zhong, Yi Sun, Shuoyang Sun, Jiahui Wang, Bin Chen, Shu-Tao Xia, Xuan Wang

item.title: Parabolic Positional Encoding: A Vision-Centric, Principled, Extrapolatable, and General Approach
item.description: arXiv:2602.01418v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose Parabolic Positional Encoding (PaPE), a parabola-based positional encoding for vision modalities in attention-based architectures. Given a set of vision tokens-such as from videos, event camera streams, images, or point clouds-our objective is to encode their positions while accounting for the characteristics of vision modalities. Prior works have largely extended positional encodings from 1D-sequences in language to nD-structures in vision, but only with partial account of vision characteristics. We address this gap by designing PaPE from principles distilled from prior work: translation invariance, rotation invariance (PaPE-RI), distance decay, directionality, and context awareness. Extrapolation experiments on ImageNet-1K show how PaPE extrapolates remarkably well, improving in absolute terms by up to 10.5 over the next-best encoding. Generality experiments on 8 datasets across 4 modalities show that PaPE is a general vision positional encoding, as PaPE matches the best baseline on 5 datasets and exceeds all on 2 datasets. The code is available at https://github.com/DTU-PAS/parabolic-position-encoding.
item.dc:creator: Christoffer Koo {\O}hrstr{\o}m, Rafael I. Cabral Muchacho, Yifei Dong, Filippos Moumtzidellis, Ronja G\"uldenring, Florian T. Pokorny, Lazaros Nalpantidis

item.title: AdaGS: Confidence-Gated Diffusion Adaptation for Unposed Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Reconstruction
item.description: arXiv:2602.21535v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Sparse-view outdoor 3D reconstruction remains challenging for Gaussian splatting. Although diffusion restorers can provide additional pseudo-view supervision, we identify a failure pattern in diffusion-guided reconstruction: an unguided diffusion model may misinterpret floating artifacts and complete them into plausible but non-existent scene structures. To mitigate this challenge, we propose a confidence-gated diffusion adaptation framework for unposed sparse-view reconstruction. We introduce an artifact-aware adapter that is trained in two stages on our constructed Gaussian artifact dataset. The adapter suppresses floater-induced visual cues before diffusion restoration, while bidirectional confidence fusion accepts generated regions only when they are supported by cross-view geometric evidence. Furthermore, we introduce a Gaussian stabilization strategy to attenuate Gaussians that exhibit weak multi-view inconsistency, preventing them from repeatedly triggering hallucinations in later optimization. Extensive experiments on three outdoor datasets demonstrate that our method improves rendering fidelity and pose accuracy over existing approaches.
item.dc:creator: Beizhen Zhao, Sicheng Yu, Guanzhi Ding, Yu Hu, Hao Wang

item.title: Generalizable Multiscale Segmentation of Heterogeneous Map Collections
item.description: arXiv:2603.05037v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Historical map collections are highly diverse in style, scale, and geographic focus, often consisting of many single-sheet documents. Yet most work in map recognition focuses on specialist models tailored to homogeneous map series. In contrast, this article aims to develop generalizable semantic segmentation models and a shared class ontology. We introduce Semap, a new open benchmark dataset comprising 1,439 manually annotated patches designed to reflect the variety of historical map documents. We also evaluate a segmentation workflow that combines procedural data synthesis with multiscale integration. Under the harmonized benchmarks considered here, this workflow attains the strongest performance among the evaluated approaches and viably learns from heterogeneous map data. The results indicate that segmentation performance remains largely stable across map collections, scales, geographic regions, and publication contexts. By providing benchmark data, a shared ontology, and an evaluation of generic segmentation across heterogeneous maps, this work contributes toward integrating the long tail of cartographic archives into historical geographic studies.
item.dc:creator: Remi Petitpierre

item.title: Place-it-R1: Unlocking Environment-aware Reasoning Potential of MLLM for Video Object Insertion
item.description: arXiv:2603.06140v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Video object insertion is fundamental to video editing, yet existing diffusion methods often produce visually plausible but physically inconsistent results. We present Place-it-R1, an end-to-end framework for physically plausible video object insertion driven by environment-aware MLLM reasoning. Rather than treating reasoning as a generic text prompt, Place-it-R1 uses the MLLM to analyze the target environment, infer object-scene interactions, and determine where an insertion is physically valid. The resulting reasoning is translated into two complementary forms of guidance for video diffusion: semantic guidance that describes the intended physical interaction and spatial guidance that provides a valid insertion region in each frame. To further align generation with local physical realism, we introduce Spatial Direct Preference Optimization, which leverages an MLLM to rank generated candidates, and introduces a region-aware preference objective that explicitly localizes physical-violation penalties to the inserted-object region. Place-it-R1 further offers flexible and standard modes to trade off environment adaptation and scene preservation. Extensive experiments show that Place-it-R1 produces more physically coherent and visually natural insertions than state-of-the-art methods and achieves competitive results against commercial systems.
item.dc:creator: Bohai Gu, Taiyi Wu, Dazhao Du, Jian Liu, Shuai Yang, Xiaotong Zhao, Alan Zhao, Song Guo

item.title: SUREON: A Benchmark and Vision-Language Model for Surgical Reasoning
item.description: arXiv:2603.06570v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A capable surgical AI model should reason from visual evidence; yet, many existing surgical benchmarks can be partially solved without visual input, as models may exploit procedural priors or common anatomy-instrument interactions to infer answers from language alone. To address this, we introduce SUREON, a video question-answering (QA) dataset and benchmark designed to evaluate visually grounded surgical reasoning. Our pipeline generates QA pairs from narrated surgical academic videos, refines incorrect options using multiple models to reduce linguistic biases, and uses trained adversarial guessers to filter out questions answerable without visual evidence. The resulting dataset contains 76K training pairs covering 168 procedures and 10 specialties, alongside a benchmark of 340 questions across 10 categories verified by expert surgeons. Benchmarking leading commercial and open-source models shows that surgical visual reasoning remains largely unsolved--no model exceeds 53% accuracy and even expert surgeons reach only 64.9%. We also introduce SUREON-VLM, a baseline trained on our curated data that avoids language shortcuts, outperforms existing open-source models on SUREON, and matches larger specialist models on multiple standard surgical benchmarks. Our training ablations show that distractor refinement and blind curation strengthen visual grounding, increasing the multimodal gain from 8.7 to 29.1 percentage points while reducing the training set from 176.6K to 76K filtered samples. SUREON thus offers both a verified testbed for surgical visual reasoning and training data that strengthens visual grounding.
item.dc:creator: Alejandra Perez, Anita Rau, Busisiwe Mlambo, Lee White, Aina Brunet, Juan Verde, Juan Caicedo, Jo\"el L. Lavanchy, Adam Schmidt, Chinedu Nwoye, Omid Mohareri, Muhammad Abdullah Jamal

item.title: Autoregressive Diffusion for Compositional Text-to-Scene Generation
item.description: arXiv:2604.16552v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent text-to-scene generation approaches largely reduced the manual efforts required to create 3D scenes. However, their focus is either to generate a scene layout or to generate objects, and few generate both. The generated scene layout is often simple even with LLM's help. Moreover, the generated scene is often inconsistent with the text input that contains non-trivial descriptions of the shape, appearance, and spatial arrangement of the objects. We present a new paradigm of sequential text-to-scene generation and propose a novel generative model for interactive scene creation. At the core is a 3D Autoregressive Diffusion model 3D-ARD+, which unifies the autoregressive generation over a multimodal token sequence and diffusion generation of next-object 3D latents. To generate the next object, the model uses one autoregressive step to generate the coarse-grained 3D latents in the scene space, conditioned on both the current seen text instructions and already synthesized 3D scene. It then uses a second step to generate the 3D latents in the smaller object space, which can be decoded into fine-grained object geometry and appearance. We curate a large dataset of 230K indoor scenes with paired text instructions for training. We evaluate 7B 3D-ARD+, on challenging scenes, and showcase the model can generate and place objects following non-trivial spatial layout and semantics prescribed by the text instructions.
item.dc:creator: Zhenggang Tang, Yuehao Wang, Yuchen Fan, Jun-Kun Chen, Yu-Ying Yeh, Kihyuk Sohn, Zhangyang Wang, Qixing Huang, Alexander Schwing, Rakesh Ranjan, Dilin Wang, Zhicheng Yan

item.title: MuCALD-SplitFed: Causal-Latent Diffusion for Privacy-Preserving Multi-Task Split-Federated Medical Image Segmentation
item.description: arXiv:2605.04108v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Federated Learning enables decentralized training by aggregating model updates across clients without sharing raw data, while Split Federated Learning further partitions the model between clients and a server to reduce computation and communication at the client side. However, decentralized medical institutions rarely operate on a single shared task, making standard Federated and SplitFed collaborations poorly aligned with real clinical workflows. Multi-task FL extends these frameworks by allowing clients to handle different tasks, but often introduces instability and privacy vulnerabilities. This study proposes \textbf{MuCALD-SplitFed}, a multi-task SplitFed framework that integrates causal representation learning and latent diffusion. Experiments show MuCALD-SplitFed consistently improves segmentation, while baseline SplitFed fails to converge. The proposed approach further reduces information leakage at split points, mitigating reconstruction-based and membership inference attacks. Additionally, MuCALD SplitFed outperforms state-of-the-art personalized FL and multi-task FL approaches. The code repository is: https://github.com/ChamaniS/MuCALD_SplitFed.
item.dc:creator: Chamani Shiranthika, Hadi Hadizadeh, Parvaneh Saeedi

item.title: Sparkle: Realizing Lively Instruction-Guided Video Background Replacement via Decoupled Guidance
item.description: arXiv:2605.06535v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In recent years, open-source efforts like Senorita-2M have propelled video editing toward natural language instruction. However, current publicly available datasets predominantly focus on local editing or style transfer, which largely preserve the original scene structure and are easier to scale. In contrast, Background Replacement, a task central to creative applications such as film production and advertising, requires synthesizing entirely new, temporally consistent scenes while maintaining accurate foreground-background interactions, making large-scale data generation significantly more challenging. Consequently, this complex task remains largely underexplored due to a scarcity of high-quality training data. This gap is evident in poorly performing state-of-the-art models, e.g., Kiwi-Edit, because the primary open-source dataset that contains this task, i.e., OpenVE-3M, frequently produces static, unnatural backgrounds. In this paper, we trace this quality degradation to a lack of precise background guidance during data synthesis. Accordingly, we design a scalable pipeline that generates foreground and background guidance in a decoupled manner with strict quality filtering. Building on this pipeline, we introduce Sparkle, a dataset of ~140K video pairs spanning five common background-change themes, alongside Sparkle-Bench, the largest evaluation benchmark tailored for background replacement to date. Experiments demonstrate that our dataset and the model trained on it achieve substantially better performance than all existing baselines on both OpenVE-Bench and Sparkle-Bench. Our proposed dataset, benchmark, model, as well as the full data generation pipeline, are fully open-sourced at https://showlab.github.io/Sparkle/.
item.dc:creator: Ziyun Zeng, Yiqi Lin, Guoqiang Liang, Mike Zheng Shou

item.title: DRScaffold: Boosting Dense-Scene Reasoning in Lightweight Vision Language Models
item.description: arXiv:2605.26038v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Lightweight vision-language models perform competitively on standard benchmarks yet fail systematically in dense-scene reasoning, where multiple objects, attributes, and relations must be jointly grounded and resolved through multi-step inference. Such capability is critical for real-world applications where models must reliably interpret cluttered environments. Yet existing training signals provide no explicit grounding between reasoning steps and the underlying visual entities and relations, leaving lightweight models free to generate fluent but visually unanchored reasoning chains. To address this gap, we first introduce DRBench, a benchmark of 14,573 questions across 2,943 images, organized into five task categories spanning three progressive reasoning layers. Building on DRBench, we propose DRScaffold, a supervised fine-tuning framework that decomposes the supervision target into four causally ordered stages, promoting grounded reasoning without architectural modification. Experiments on three lightweight VLMs demonstrate substantial gains on DRBench while preserving or improving performance on general-purpose benchmarks. Notably, Qwen2.5-VL-3B trained with DRScaffold surpasses the frozen Qwen2.5-VL-32B under zero-shot direct-answer prompting on DRBench, demonstrating that structured supervision can substitute for a significant portion of model scale in dense-scene reasoning. Our code is available at https://github.com/irene-shi/DRScaffold.
item.dc:creator: Xinrui Shi, Kai Liu, Ziqing Zhang, Jianze Li, Anqi Li, Yulun Zhang

item.title: Analyzing the Optimization Conflict Between Image- and Text-Based Person Re-Identification
item.description: arXiv:2606.02242v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Unifying image-based (I2I) and text-based (T2I) person re-identification (ReID) within a single model is complicated by a fundamental conflict between their training objectives. While I2I ReID focuses on identity-level invariance across images of the same person captured by multiple cameras, T2I ReID is driven by instance-specific textual descriptions tied to unique visual traits. When both objectives are optimized on a shared vision encoder, they impose opposing requirements on the same embeddings - I2I contracts intra-identity distances while T2I requires them to persist - so improving one task's representation actively degrades the other's. This paper analyzes this optimization conflict and shows empirically that the two objectives are not jointly satisfiable by a single unconstrained encoder. Motivated by this finding, we investigate the conflict through a controlled two-stage pipeline: a shared vision encoder is first trained for I2I invariance, then frozen while only the text encoder is aligned to the fixed visual space, preventing the T2I objective from unwinding the identity-level structure already learned. We conduct extensive experiments across multiple configurations, varying domain-mixing procedures, learning strategies, and task objectives. We observe that I2I pre-training improves subsequent T2I performance, while textual supervision during this pre-training further improves T2I performance, although the vision encoder is frozen during subsequent cross-modal training. We believe these insights provide a meaningful step toward unified ReID systems that reconcile identity-level and instance-level supervision within a single representation.
item.dc:creator: Karina Kvanchiani, Timur Mamedov

item.title: How Do Video Foundation Models Encode Intuitive Physics? Probing Across Pretraining Paradigms
item.description: arXiv:2606.09646v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Do video foundation models encode a usable sense of how the physical world works, and does intuitive physics emerge naturally from large-scale video pretraining? In this work, we study whether pretrained video foundation models encode intuitive-physics information in their frozen representations, and how its accessibility varies across pretraining paradigms, layers, backbone variants, and probe types. Using frozen-feature probing on IntPhys2 and Minimal Video Pairs (MVP), we compare predictive joint-embedding models (V-JEPA), masked reconstruction models (VideoMAE), and diffusion-based video generators (LTX-Video). We find that across linear, MLP, and temporal attentive probes, physics-relevant information is generally weakest in early layers and most accessible at intermediate to late depth. On MVP, temporal attentive probes substantially outperform linear readouts, with V-JEPA achieving 95.0% pair consistency. On IntPhys2, linear probes recover more signal, and VideoMAE attains the strongest temporal attentive result at 73.9% violation-of-expectation accuracy. On both benchmarks, attentive probe performance on LTX consistently underperforms compared to the other two pretraining paradigms. Together, these results suggest that intuitive-physics is broadly decodable from video foundation models, but it is not represented as a single, uniform capability. Its accessibility, and especially its temporal grounding, depends much more on the benchmark and readout than on a simple hierarchy of pretraining objectives or model scale.
item.dc:creator: Samuele Punzo, Niccol\`o Caselli, Ippokratis Pantelidis, Francesco Massafra, Salvatore Lo Sardo, Mohammadreza Salehi

item.title: A Lightweight Fiducial-Based Pipeline for 3D Hyperspectral Mapping of ex-vivo Lumpectomy Specimens
item.description: arXiv:2606.14534v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Hyperspectral Imaging (HSI) is a promising modality for intraoperative assessment of resection margins in Breast-Conserving Surgery (BCS), but its clinical translation requires aligning the inherently 2D spectral information onto the 3D shape of the excised tissue so that suspicious regions can be precisely localized for targeted follow-up. We present a fully automated, calibration-free pipeline that produces a 3D hyperspectral point cloud of an ex-vivo lumpectomy specimen from a set of consumer-camera RGB images and a single top-down HSI acquisition. The 3D geometry is reconstructed with a deep-learning Structure-from-Motion backbone, stabilized in a metric reference frame by a custom bundle adjustment that enforces consistency on the corners of four ArUco markers placed around the specimen. The HSI cube is then registered to the reconstruction without recovering the HSI camera pose: the markers, visible in both modalities, define 16 corner correspondences that drive a planar homography, and 3D coordinates are recovered by lookup on an orthographically rendered depth map. Evaluated on two ex-vivo lumpectomy specimens, the pipeline achieves a median 3D registration error below 1 mm and a 2D reprojection error below 0.02 mm, with a total per-specimen processing time under 4 minutes on accelerated hardware. These results support the feasibility of integrating HSI-guided spatial localization into intraoperative margin assessment workflows for breast-conserving surgery.
item.dc:creator: Anna Bicchi, Alberto Rota, Leonardo Passoni, Nicola Ancellotti, Andrea Peroni, Lorenzo Vinco, Andrea Rabolini, Arianna Bonizzi, Carlo Francesco Morasso, Fabrizio Preda, Renzo Vanna, Dario Polli, Elena De Momi

item.title: PRISM: Feed-Forward Single-Image 3D Reconstruction via Geometric Warp-Residual Modeling
item.description: arXiv:2606.25430v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Reconstructing 3D scenes from a single image is a fundamental challenge in computer vision, with broad applications in virtual reality, robotics, and content creation. Recent methods achieve outstanding performance by leveraging camera-controlled video diffusion models, but rely on iterative diffusion sampling, which greatly limits their practical deployment. We observe that geometric forward warping alone can cover the majority of a target view directly from the input image, with only a compact residual left for the encoder to correct. Motivated by this observation, we propose PRISM, a feed-forward framework that decomposes multi-view latent prediction into a parameter-free geometric prior and a learned residual correction, with no diffusion sampling required at inference. To enable generalization from purely synthetic training data, we devise a two-stage training strategy combining latents supervised distillation for geometric generalization and perceptual fine-tuning for appearance quality optimization. Extensive experiments on three benchmarks demonstrate that PRISM achieves competitive reconstruction quality compared with diffusion-based methods, while reducing inference time dramatically to only 36 seconds per scene. Our code is available at https://github.com/microjie372/PRISM.
item.dc:creator: Zhijie Zheng, Xinhao Xiang, Jiawei Zhang

item.title: Soft Mixture-of-Recursions: Going Deeper with Recursive Vision Transformers
item.description: arXiv:2607.00774v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Vision Transformers are typically scaled by increasing depth or width, at the cost of more unique parameters. We explore recursion as an alternative scaling axis that increases effective computational depth through parameter reuse. Yet simply increasing recursion depth does not reliably improve performance because representations from different recursion stages are not fully utilized. We propose Soft Mixture-of-Recursions (SoftMoR), which learns token-wise weights to combine representations across recursion steps, and instantiate it as the Soft Recursive Vision Transformer (SR-ViT). Experiments on ImageNet-1K, COCO, and ADE20K show that SR-ViT can benefit from deeper recursion while adding few parameters. On ImageNet-1K, increasing recursion depth from T=1 to T=3 improves top-1 accuracy from 79.83% to 82.45% with only 1.1M additional parameters. At matched effective depth, SR-ViT also outperforms independently parameterized counterparts with substantially fewer parameters. These results support recursive deepening as an effective, parameter-efficient scaling axis for Vision Transformers. The code is available at https://github.com/sangin-lee/sr-vit .
item.dc:creator: Sang In Lee, Jihun Park

item.title: Fields of the Planet: Field Boundary Mapping Beyond 10m
item.description: arXiv:2607.04449v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Field-boundary accuracy depends on the model, sensor resolution, label discretization, and evaluation procedure. Measuring the contribution of sensor resolution therefore requires a controlled comparison across sensors. We present Fields of the Planet (FTP), a 3 m PlanetScope companion to Fields of The World (FTW) containing 133,168 co-registered patch-window targets across 24 countries. FTP preserves FTW's vector polygons, seasonal windows, and dataset splits, enabling direct comparison with 10 m Sentinel-2. We first quantify the resolution ceiling by rasterizing and vectorizing the same ground-truth parcels at each resolution to determine which fields the label grid can represent. We evaluate predicted parcels with polygon-level and boundary metrics. With identical PRUE+ training and post-processing across sensors, plus an upsampled Sentinel-2 control, we isolate gains from image content. PlanetScope raises panoptic quality (PQ) from 21.0 to 35.5, improves PQ on sub-$0.5$ ha fields from 5.8 to 15.7, and reduces matched-boundary error from 18.6 m to 7.4 m. Pixel-level metrics understate this improvement, so field-boundary benchmarks should account for sensor resolution.
item.dc:creator: Isaac Corley, Caleb Robinson, Hannah Kerner, Jennifer Marcus

item.title: NanoVSR: Towards Real-Time Video Super-Resolution on Edge Devices
item.description: arXiv:2607.10495v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent Video Super-Resolution (VSR) methods rely heavily on transformers and explicit optical flow, creating computational overhead and custom operations that hinder deployment on hardware accelerators like TensorRT. To address this, we introduce NanoVSR, a scalable, fully convolutional architecture designed for resource-constrained edge devices. Using structural reparameterization, NanoVSR collapses into standard convolutions during inference, ensuring seamless hardware compatibility and negligible runtime overhead. Furthermore, despite lacking explicit motion compensation, it maintains competitive restoration quality by implicitly learning spatio-temporal alignments through progressive training. Evaluated on the REDS4 benchmark, NanoVSR demonstrates an exceptional balance between accuracy and computational efficiency, significantly improving the trade-off for compact architectures. Our NanoVSR-644k baseline yields 28.64 dB PSNR while delivering 27.2 FPS on the NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX 16GB (25W), offering massive speed gains over heavier models. The scaled NanoVSR-1.7M variant reaches 29.15 dB with a throughput of 19.58 FPS, providing superior, edge-optimized upscaling. Code is available at https://github.com/filippawlicki/nanovsr.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Computer Vision - ECCV 2026, LNCS, pp. 620-639, Springer, 2026
item.dc:creator: Filip Pawlicki, Marcel Ka\'ndu{\l}a, Marcin Pucek, Kamil Dobies

item.title: DAUPNet: Domain-Aware Uncertainty Modeling for Reliable Prototype Discrimination in Cross-Domain Few-Shot Semantic Segmentation
item.description: arXiv:2607.16308v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Cross-domain few-shot semantic segmentation (CD-FSS) has predominantly been formulated as learning domain-invariant representations or improving support-query correspondence. Nevertheless, large domain shifts still make prototype matching unreliable: inconsistent hierarchical responses corrupt the support representation, deterministic prototypes cannot express boundary and appearance ambiguity, and treating prototypes with different reliability equally during optimization weakens foreground-background separation. We therefore propose DAUPNet, a unified framework that reformulates cross-domain prototype matching as uncertainty-aware prototype discrimination. DAUPNet first harmonizes hierarchical support-query features to provide stable evidence, then represents foreground and background prototypes probabilistically, and finally uses their estimated uncertainty to regulate contrastive optimization. On four standard target domains, DAUPNet achieves 72.6% and 76.7% average mIoU in the 1-shot and 5-shot settings, respectively, including substantial gains on the two medical domains. These results demonstrate that modeling prototype uncertainty and incorporating it into optimization provides a robust and interpretable approach to CD-FSS under severe domain shift. The code is available at https://github.com/madness-Lei/DAUPNet
item.dc:creator: Lei Yuan, Zhongxu Hu, Jingyi Wen, Pengxing Yi

item.title: IR275K: A Benchmark for Infrared Multi-Frame Super-Resolution Toward Efficient Remote Sensing
item.description: arXiv:2607.22380v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Infrared multi-frame super-resolution (MFSR) exploits complementary observations to recover spatial detail, but its evaluation remains fragmented across datasets and protocols. A common benchmark is needed to evaluate reconstruction under weak texture, varying thermal contrast, and noise in the source imagery. It should also characterize reconstruction performance across different inter-frame displacement ranges. We introduce IR275K, a curated benchmark containing 594 in- frared video sequences and 275,196 frames. It provides sequence- level train/validation/test splits and a reproducible x4 evaluation protocol. Evaluation spans single-frame and multi-frame recon- struction using seven learned baselines, the CGMamba reference model, and bicubic interpolation. All learned methods are evalu- ated under both bicubic degradation and synthetic mixed sensor noise.EDVRleadstheoverallrankingunderbicubicdegradation, whereas MSDTGP leads under mixed sensor noise. DBSR leads thehigh-displacementUAVsubsetunderbothsettings.Controlled ablations using CGMamba show that real neighboring frames improve PSNR over center-frame repetition by 1.04 dB under bicubic degradation and 0.95 dB under mixed sensor noise. Center-frame conditioning also improves reconstruction under both settings. The benchmark thus reveals how reconstruction rankings and the benefits of neighboring frames depend on evaluation conditions. The complete IR275K dataset is publicly available at: https://github.com/InfraRecon7/IR275K.

item.title: GUI-Lens: Enabling Precise GUI Grounding for Off-the-Shelf VLMs via Coarse-to-Fine Cropping
item.description: arXiv:2608.03270v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: GUI grounding maps natural-language instructions to click locations and is essential for reliable GUI agents. The task remains difficult on high-resolution, densely populated interfaces because a vision-language model (VLM) may recognize a requested control without locating it precisely enough for interaction. Most existing methods provide various forms of localization assistance, but still rely on a direct click prediction, allowing visual ambiguity or an inaccurate initial estimate to propagate to the final result. In this paper, we introduce GUI-Lens, a coarse-to-fine grounding framework that allows a general-purpose VLM to determine the target through active visual observations. Specifically, GUI-Lens extracts OCR text and detected UI components from the screenshot and presents their positions as coordinate references. Using the instruction, the current view, and these references, the VLM selects the region and scale of the next view, which is cropped and enlarged to provide finer visual details. This process continues over successively focused views until the target is determined. Proposed crops and clicks are checked against the instruction throughout the process, and the final local position is mapped back to the original screen coordinates. Experiments on five GUI grounding benchmarks and six general-purpose base models show that GUI-Lens consistently improves grounding accuracy, achieving up to 9.3 times the accuracy of direct grounding on ScreenSpot-Pro.

item.title: HOPE: Hand-Object Pressure Estimation from Monocular Videos
item.description: arXiv:2608.06192v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Estimating physical pressure from vision is essential for understanding contact-rich hand-object interaction. However, prior vision-based pressure estimation methods are largely limited to planar surfaces and single image input, making them difficult to apply to dynamic hand-object interaction with diverse objects. We instead formulate pressure estimation as a hand-centric video prediction problem with monocular video as input. This formulation predicts temporally evolving per-vertex normal pressure and contact directly on the hand mesh, yielding a unified output space independent of object shape and sensor layout. Building on this formulation, we propose \textbf{HOPE}, a framework with two key components. First, we lift tactile-glove pressure, planar-sensor pressure, and distance-based hand-object contact annotations into a shared hand vertex space, allowing bare-hand contact data to regularize pressure learning where labels are unavailable. Second, we introduce a vertex-anchored video transformer that treats each vertex as a persistent token, aggregates visual features and hand pose over time, and uses a contact-gated pressure head to suppress pressure predictions in regions with low contact probability. Experiments on OpenTouch, PressureVisionDB, and hand-object contact benchmarks validate HOPE across object-pressure, surface-pressure, and contact-supervised HOI settings. Despite using pressure supervision primarily from gloved-hand videos, HOPE generalizes to bare-hand egocentric and in-the-wild videos, producing joint contact and pressure predictions beyond the scope of contact-only or planar-pressure baselines.

item.title: SV-WAM: An Efficient Surround-View World-Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
item.description: arXiv:2609.03602v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: World models (WMs) have demonstrated strong potential for end-to-end autonomous driving by learning predictive representations of future scene dynamics. However, generating future videos during inference introduces substantial computational overhead, leading many recent driving WMs to adopt a single front camera as input for efficient deployment. This design restricts spatial coverage in safety-critical maneuvers such as lane changes, merges, and turns. To address this limitation, we propose SV-WAM, a surround-view world-action model (WAM) that preserves full six-camera observations while maintaining efficient inference. SV-WAM leverages future-video prediction as dense training supervision for action learning within a shared generative model, rather than as an inference-time output. At the core of this design is an action-centered causal mask that prevents action tokens from attending to future-video tokens during joint action-video denoising. Consequently, the video branch can be discarded at deployment, enabling efficient action-only planning. Furthermore, we introduce a differentiable drivable-area compliance regularizer that penalizes vehicle-footprint corners approaching or crossing drivable boundaries, improving planning safety and boundary awareness. Extensive experiments on the closed-loop NAVSIMv2 benchmark and the open-loop nuScenes benchmark demonstrate that SV-WAM achieves state-of-the-art planning performance with low inference latency and competitive zero-shot transfer capability.

item.title: DRT: Dense Reasoning Trace for Efficient and Grounded Multimodal Reasoning
item.description: arXiv:2609.21675v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Despite the remarkable progress in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), prevailing Chain-of-Thought (CoT) paradigms remain confined to the natural-language expression space. Consequently, they inherently incur excessive linguistic overhead, leading to information dilution and weak visual grounding. To address this challenge, we propose Dense Reasoning Trace (DRT), a paradigm that departs from natural-language-centered CoT by expressing reasoning as compact structured traces, which include concise intermediate states with symbolic connectors and disentangle visual observations from logical deductions. First, we introduce the Dense Trace Initialization to internalize the DRT reasoning mode into the model, substantially improving token efficiency while preserving visual evidence. To further enable the model to faithfully capture the logical relations within traces, we propose the Trace-Grounded Reinforcement Learning framework, which builds reference traces through a tri-perspective verification pipeline and employs Trace-Grounded GRPO with structured rewards, encouraging the model to generate concise DRT-style traces with reduced hallucination and stronger logical grounding. Extensive experiments on challenging reasoning benchmarks show that DRT achieves 5.5$\times$ token efficiency improvement while improving 1.3 accuracy points over the Qwen3-VL baseline. These findings suggest that complex multimodal reasoning may not require verbose natural-language traces, opening a more efficient path for next-generation MLLMs. Our code and data are available at: https://github.com/HIT-leaderone/DRT

item.title: One Step Is Optimal: Unconditional Rectified Flows as Noise2Noise Denoisers for Low-Dose CT
item.description: arXiv:2609.31670v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study rectified flows for denoising without clean training targets. For an unconditional rectified flow trained on Noise2Noise pairs, the optimal velocity field yields the minimum mean squared error (MMSE) denoiser in one step. In a jointly Gaussian model, we show that integrating the flow before applying its denoising readout increases error with integration time. The flow transports between noisy distributions, so its endpoint is not a clean-image estimate. Experiments on low-dose CT and Gaussian-corrupted natural images follow this pattern: one-step flow performs similarly to direct regression on the same pairs, whereas additional Euler steps reduce PSNR. A direct regressor using spatially separated, similar patches gives our best label-free CT result, a $1.99$\,dB gain over the noisy input. We report these results in CTDenoiser, a benchmark covering five architectures, supervised and self-supervised training, and two per-image methods. Supervised CNNs gain about $4$\,dB, while label-free performance depends strongly on how training pairs account for correlated CT noise. A channelized Hotelling observer also shows that fidelity gains need not improve lesion detectability: detectability falls at $160$\,HU despite higher PSNR and SSIM, while changes at $40$--$80$\,HU are small. Code, model definitions, and data-loading utilities will be released publicly; the repository link is withheld for anonymous review.

item.title: Gaussian Splatting-based Volumetric Video Compression with Sparse 4D Anchors
item.description: arXiv:2609.33969v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Immersive video communication requires photorealistic, compact dynamic scene representations that support efficient rendering. 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) is a promising approach, but dynamic 3DGS remains difficult to compress due to its dense primitives and spatiotemporal redundancy. Anchor-based formulations improve compactness through sparse scaffolds that share geometry and appearance across primitives. However, existing designs typically deform a single canonical scaffold and condition each primitive solely on its associated anchor, limiting their ability to model non-local dynamics and disocclusions and exploit inter-anchor correlations. To address these limitations, we propose SAGA, a volumetric video codec built on Sparse Anchor-assisted GAussian splatting representations. SAGA represents a dynamic scene using hierarchical sparse anchors in 4D space-time. Coordinate-based INR decoders generate fine anchors and Gaussian primitives from features obtained through kernel interpolation among nearby anchors, enabling parameter sharing across spatiotemporal structures. A fixed-size memory with a novel orthogonality-informed slot-update strategy further captures long-range dependencies among unstructured anchors for entropy coding. Empirically, \name achieves PSNR-based BD-rate reductions of 90.88%, 64.30% and 65.14% relative to GIFStream, TED-4DGS, and OMG4, respectively, on the Neu3D testset.

item.title: Sub-Voxel Displacement and Ipsilateral Territory Decoupling for 3D Bilateral Coronary Artery Tree Reconstruction in Cardiac CT Angiography
item.description: arXiv:2610.05900v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Bilateral coronary tree (LCA/RCA) reconstruction in cardiac CT angiography (CCTA) faces $64^3$ discretization, territory ambiguity, and ostium drift. Within GT-foreground $128^3$ ROIs ($\pm 15$-voxel margin, 9.8--12.0 mm; seed-free in ROI; whole-volume localization upstream), we propose a canonical $(Z_{IS},Y_{PA},X_{LR})$ multi-task network and scalar-potential arborescence solver. Volumes, centerlines, and thick-stem ostia map to $(Z_{IS},Y_{PA},X_{LR})$, extending a 3D pyramid encoder and tubular decoder with a $128^3\to 64^3$ skip, stop-gradient $128^3$ residual branch, 3D sub-voxel displacement head $\Delta\hat{u}(x)$, ipsilateral head $(P_{LCA},P_{RCA})$, and $32^3$ ostium head. From a recall-balanced anchor, 327,385 active parameters (398,843 total) are fine-tuned in a 30-epoch AdamW loop ($\epsilon=10^{-8}$, 7 groups) with L2-SP/anchor blending. Our solver couples Valsalva-STJ calibration, $128^3$ rooting, contralateral inhibition, radius-ratio pruning, normal-plane pullback, and collision reduction. On OOS-50 (Cases 251--300, 50 volumes, 100 trees; 201--250 isolated) vs. 3D U-Net (skeleton/$M_3$--$M_5$) and 5 proxies, it reaches $2.7671\pm 1.1385$ mm $CD_{CL}^{union}$ (SD 0.0415), $3.2338\pm 1.3557$ mm $CD_{CL}^{arc1mm}$, and $3.2926\pm 2.6253$ mm $CD_{ipsi}$ (arc1mm 3.7460 mm, node $p_{Holm}\le 0.0400$ vs. Ext-0b [arc1mm $p=0.1629/0.2187$]; 76.33% junction [23.04% 1-to-1], 79.65% branch F1). On Dev-14 (14 volumes, 28 trees), it reaches $2.1362\pm 0.5041$ mm $CD_{CL}^{union}$ (SD 0.0369), $2.3798\pm 0.5725$ mm $CD_{CL}^{arc1mm}$, and $2.2480\pm 0.6835$ mm $CD_{ipsi}$ (arc1mm 2.4951 mm, node $CD_{CL}^{union}$ $p_{Holm}=0.0494$ vs. Ext-0b [$CD_{ipsi}$/arc1mm $p_{Holm}=0.1353/0.0676$--$0.0906$]; 56.76%/77.74% F1@1/2mm; 79.95% junction [21.06% 1-to-1], 83.80% branch F1, 4.6880/4.9298 mm ostia), and $N=64$ $CD_{CL}^{union}=2.6291\pm 1.0629$ mm (arc1mm 3.0470, $CD_{ipsi}$ 3.0641).

item.title: Vision Transformer Ensembles for Panoramic Street Segmentation
item.description: arXiv:2610.06063v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Semantic segmentation of street panoramas can support detailed descriptions of urban environments, yet small datasets and unequal training costs make model selection difficult. This paper documents the two stages of a submission to the PalmCity challenge. In the first stage, nine pretrained segmentation systems are compared using approximately equal computation budgets, and the two leading candidates are trained with three random seeds. An equal probability average of three Encoder only Mask Transformer models with DINOv3 features, evaluated at three image scales with horizontal reflection, reaches 60.95% mean intersection over union on the 84 image validation split and 57.08% on the hidden test leaderboard, first in the snapshot of 5 October 2026. In the second stage, color and crop augmentation, rare class sampling, larger inputs, further architectures, and post processing are tested under the same update budget, and candidates are compared through a paired image bootstrap with selection rules fixed before the results. Training at 768 by 1536 and 896 by 1792 pixels gives the largest gains. The selected ensemble of four models scores 64.53% on validation when trained on the training images alone. Retrained on the training and validation images, it receives 61.54% mean intersection over union and 71.93% mean F1 on the hidden test leaderboard, first among five entries in the snapshot of 30 October 2026. Segment Anything voting, instance mask overlays, and ensembles with other architectures all reduce the validation score. Because the validation images guided many choices and the final models were trained on them, the validation scores are optimistic and the test score is the only independent measurement. The study reports all runs, comparisons, costs, and limits, and releases the code and models.
